source_refs.note: Time period and frequency: a main subheading of 14.3 Practical S.H.M Systems, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 22-23.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The last line should read T = 1/f = 2π√(m/k): T is the reciprocal of f = (1/2π)√(k/m), so m/k comes under the root. A heavier mass gives a longer period.

blocks.title: Point to ponder!
blocks.text:
Real world applications that utilize S.H.M principle include:
• Pendulum clocks, musical instruments, and vehicle suspension system etc.

blocks.title: Example 14.1
blocks.problem: A particle executing simple harmonic motion has an angular frequency of 2 rad s⁻¹. Determine its frequency and time period.
steps:
Angular frequency ω = 2 rad s⁻¹, Frequency f = ?
Time period t = ?
blocks.answer: The frequency is approximately 0.318 Hz, and the time period is approximately 3 seconds.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: Dutch Mathematician astronomer and physicist Christiaan Huygens patented the first pendulum clock in 1656. He finalized the mathematical formula that relates pendulum length to time, using simple harmonic motion.

blocks.alt: Huygens' first pendulum clock (1656) in a tall wooden case: a dial with Roman numerals and gears at the top, and a pendulum rod with a round bob hanging below. Screws b, a and c stand on a bar at the left; screw a holds a coil spring joined to the top of the pendulum, and screw c holds a small spring and a mass m whose line runs through a ring on the rod towards B. Arrows mark the distance x on each side of the rod and the direction A. A driving weight hangs on the left.
